            About
            Keya Saxena is a PhD candidate in the School of
            Journalism and Communication and an instructor in the
            Department of Women, Gender & Sexuality Studies at the
            University of Oregon. Originally from New Delhi, Keya brings
            a critical cultural perspective to her work, weaving
            together themes of communication, social justice, and gender
            with a keen focus on transnational contexts. For her
            doctoral research, she specializes in the use of stand-up
            comedy as a tool for social justice.
            Prior to pursuing her PhD, Keya worked in strategic
            communications with the United Nations in Switzerland and
            India, focusing on social protection, child marriage,
            adolescent reproductive health, gender equity, and menstrual
            health management.

    What Students Have Said
  
  
  
    
      I valued the conversations we had about societal issues and ideas every lab. Keya made going to lab worth waking up at 7:30 every morning. She was always positive and invested in having purposeful and open conversation.
    
    
    
      I loved her passion for the subjects we went over that week. She always challenged us to think outside of the box.
    
    
    
      Brought her own background into concepts, made great examples, very personable. Super animated and made it really easy to dive into material because she made it interesting.
    
    
    
      Directions are always clearly communicated. I have ADHD and have been able to easily stay engaged in the class because the teacher leads it with a dynamic approach that alternated between lecturing,student discussion, watching videos, and exchanging knowledge.
